title: Lifestyle Strategies to Preserve Muscle and Reduce Cardiovascular Risk in Adults With Obesity Using GLP-1 Receptor Agonists
official: Lifestyle Strategies to Preserve Muscle and Reduce Cardiovascular Risk in Adults With Obesity Using GLP-1 Receptor Agonists
summary: This study will test whether adding a lifestyle program to GLP-1 medication treatment can help preserve muscle, reduce cardiovascular risk, and improve quality of life in adults with overweight or obesity. About 670 adults who are starting a GLP-1 medication for weight loss will be enrolled. Participants will be randomly assigned to either a 6-month YMCA lifestyle program that includes resistance exercise and nutrition support, or to enhanced usual care with monthly health education workshops. Study assessments will occur at baseline, 6 months, and 12 months. The main outcome is the change in appendicular lean tissue mass measured by DXA at 6 months. Other outcomes include cardiovascular risk, quality of life, bone density, total lean mass, weight loss, dietary intake, and physical activity.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 30-79 years
* Obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m²), or overweight (BMI ≥27 kg/m²) with at least one weight-related comorbidity, such as hypertension, dyslipidemia, obstructive sleep apnea, or cardiovascular disease
* Prescribed a GLP-1 receptor agonist approved for weight loss, including semaglutide, tirzepatide, or liraglutide
* Able to enroll after prescription and before initiating GLP-1 therapy or, if already taking a GLP-1 receptor agonist, able to be randomized within 3 weeks of the first dose
* Intends to continue the GLP-1 receptor agonist
* English speaking

Exclusion Criteria:

* Severe cardiovascular or pulmonary disease, including myocardial infarction, unstable angina, stroke, or transient ischemic attack within the previous 3 months
* Uncontrolled hypertension (systolic blood pressure \>180 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure \>110 mmHg)
* Musculoskeletal or neurologic deficits that preclude exercise training
* Cognitive impairment, defined as a Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score \<23
* Treatment with a GLP-1 receptor agonist or other weight-loss medication within 6 months before screening, other than the current qualifying GLP-1 initiation
* Planned bariatric surgery or weight-loss device implantation during the study period
* Known or suspected alcohol or recreational drug abuse
* Residence in a nursing home
* Weight \>450 lb because of DXA scanner limitations
* Unable to safely complete study assessments based on investigator judgment
* Medical history that, based on physician assessment, would compromise participant safety or study fidelity
* Failure to provide informed consent
* Participation in moderate-to-high-intensity resistance training at least 1 day per week
* Another household member already enrolled in the study
